chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Ali ibn Asbat who said:

Ibn Faddal asked Ibn Bukayr in the mosque, saying: 'What do you say about a woman who breastfed a boy for two years, then breastfed a girl for less than two years, until the two years were completed? Does that invalidate the relationship between them?' He said: 'That does not invalidate the relationship between them, because it is breastfeeding after weaning. And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is no breastfeeding after weaning.' Meaning, when two years are completed for the boy or the girl, they have exited the limit of milk, and it does not invalidate the relationship between him and anyone who drinks from his milk. He said: 'And our companions say that it does not invalidate unless the boy and the girl drink sip by sip.'
ai.seo_question: Does breastfeeding after a child reaches two years of age establish a mahram relationship?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani highlights the juristic debate regarding the temporal limit of breastfeeding (radha') for establishing mahram relationships, specifically addressing whether nursing after the completion of two years invalidates the bond. It contrasts the view that weaning severs the milk bond with the opinion of the companions (Ashabuna) that continued direct suckling post-weaning may still be effective, reflecting the nuanced application of the Hadith of 'no breastfeeding after weaning' in Shia fiqh.
